events.description: The observed map name changed between two known map snapshots.
events.when: Both snapshots contain a map and their map names differ. A first map observation or disappearing map is not enough to produce this event. A map-context change establishes a new baseline for local gameplay deltas.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous and current observed map names, such as de_mirage and de_vertigo.

events.notes: This is not match_started. Loading a map does not establish that a competitive match has begun.

events.description: The normalized match phase changed within the same known map and mode.
events.when: Both map names and modes match, both phases are known, and the phase differs. The normalized vocabulary is warmup, live, intermission and game_over, not Valve's raw gameover spelling.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous and current phase: warmup, live, intermission or game_over.

events.notes: Intermission is a phase, not a match end. Changing map or losing map context does not guarantee a phase event. Match and round boundary events may accompany this event in the same source update.

events.description: An observed warmup transitioned to live play.
events.when: Within the same known map and mode, match phase changes from warmup to live. Joining an already-live match does not synthesize a match_started event.
events.notes: No event-specific fields. The transition establishes a gameplay baseline; it does not manufacture kills or another round_started. Use ctx.current_match for the retained match observation, not an assumed complete history.

events.description: Observed live play transitioned directly to game_over.
events.when: Within the same known map and mode, match phase changes from live to game_over. A disconnect, map disappearance or intermission is not this semantic event.
events.notes: No event-specific fields. It can share a payload with the final round_ended, score_changed and local stat changes, even when round.phase is already freeze_time. It does not provide a surrender reason or prove all earlier rounds were observed. Read your retained totals for this match and their final/last-observed provenance in ctx.current_match.local_summary.

events.description: The observed round phase changed in a comparable match context.
events.when: The same known map/mode is retained, both round phases are known and different, and this is not a match-start/restart baseline. Values are freeze_time, live and over.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous and current normalized round phase: freeze_time, live or over.

events.notes: A phase change alone is not a guaranteed round start or end. The stricter round_started/round_ended events verify match phase and completed-round evidence. Do not count every freeze_time transition as a new round, particularly at game over.

events.description: An observed freeze period ended and the real round became live.
events.when: Both match phases are live, round phase changes from freeze_time to live, and the known completed-round counter is unchanged. The same map/mode must be retained and this must not be a restart/start baseline.
events.notes: No event-specific fields. round.completed_rounds counts finished rounds, not the number of the round being played. A first observation already in live play does not fabricate a start event. Consult ctx.current_match.current_round for the recorder's round observation.

events.description: A previously-live round has supported completion evidence.
events.when: The previous match and round are live. The new match is live, intermission or game_over, and either (1) the new round phase is over with the known completed counter unchanged or advanced by one, or (2) the match becomes game_over and that counter advances by exactly one, even if the round phase is already freeze_time. The same map/mode must be retained without a restart/start baseline.
events.notes: No event-specific fields. winner can still be unknown, and score/counter updates can arrive later. Do not require round.phase == over in your handler: the final game-over shape can use freeze_time. The recorder retains the correct round and accepts late boundary updates; no extra round is synthesized after game over. Local stats may come from earlier authoritative observations even if the boundary is spectating a teammate. Use the retained round, not an assumed local player at the boundary.

events.description: At least one known CT/T score changed.
events.when: The same known map/mode is retained without a match-start/restart baseline. At least one side has different numeric scores in both snapshots. Each side is compared independently.

fields.name: ct
fields.description: CT score change, or null if unchanged or not comparable.

fields.name: t
fields.description: T score change, or null if unchanged or not comparable.

events.notes: CT:T describes sides, not fixed rosters. A halftime relabel such as 2:6 -> 6:2 can produce positive and negative changes without awarding six points. This is not a standalone points-won event. Use retained rounds and side_swap_before for round progression. An unknown/unchanged side is null (Rhai unit), not a zero delta. Both sides may change in the same event.

events.description: The verified local player's observed activity changed.
events.when: The previous and current snapshots both identify the same authoritative local player, and both activities are known and different. Values are menu, playing and text_input (normalized from Valve textinput). This comparison can happen even when map context changes.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous and current observed activity: menu, playing or text_input.

events.notes: A spectator target's activity is not attributed to the local player. This is not a chat-message event; text_input does not provide typed text.

events.description: The verified local player's side changed between CT and T.
events.when: Comparable same-map/mode snapshots identify the same authoritative local player; both teams are known and differ. Match-start/restart baselines do not emit this event.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous and current local side: ct or t.

events.notes: A side switch resets player-delta comparisons for this source update; health, ammo and stat changes are not inferred across it. Side switch is not evidence of a kill, death or awarded point. Match/round/score events may still accompany it. It does not describe teammate roster changes.

events.description: The local player's observed health changed within a comparable round.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both health values are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current health and signed delta. A decrease is not a damage-dealt event.

events.notes: The event does not identify an attacker, damage source or damage dealt to another player. Reaching zero alone is not enough for player_died; death also needs a corroborating increment in your player's death counter for this match.

events.description: The local player's observed armor changed within a comparable round.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both armor values are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current armor and signed delta.

events.notes: An armor change does not establish whether damage, a purchase or another game mechanic caused it. Unknown armor is not known zero.

events.description: The local player's known helmet flag changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both helmet flags are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current helmet possession. There is no numeric delta.

events.notes: The flag describes observed equipment, not an explicit purchase, sale or destruction event.

events.description: The local player's known defuse-kit flag changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both defuse-kit flags are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current defuse-kit possession. There is no numeric delta.

events.notes: This is equipment state, not a bomb-defuse event. No bomb planter, defuse progress or defuse result is included.

events.description: The local player's observed in-game money changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both money values are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current CS2 money and signed delta; not Twitch points or necko7 inventory.

events.notes: The delta does not identify its cause. Purchases, kill rewards and round economy can all affect money; do not infer a kill from money alone.

events.description: The local player's reported equipment value changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both equipment values are known and different.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current reported CS2 equipment value and signed delta.

events.notes: This is not a purchase list or inventory transaction. Missing weapons are not proof that items were dropped, and this value does not reveal which item changed.

events.description: One reported local flash, smoke or burning exposure value changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and both values for the named effect are known and different. A payload changing several effects can emit several exposure_changed events.

fields.name: effect
fields.description: Exactly flash, smoke or burning.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current reported exposure value for that effect and signed delta.

events.notes: Treat these as reported exposure units, not documented seconds, damage, a grenade entity or an attacker identity. A positive value is not a promise of any particular physical effect duration.

events.description: One or more counters for your player in the current CS2 match changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold. Every changed counter known in both snapshots is included; unchanged/unknown counters are omitted from changes.

fields.name: changes
fields.description: Non-empty changes for kills, deaths, assists, mvps and/or score accumulated by your player in this match (all rounds so far). Each entry contains stat, previous, current and signed delta.

events.notes: These are totals for this match, not this round, stream, project or lifetime. They are CS2-reported values, not counters starting when necko7 connected. Negative corrections are reported here; if any comparable match counter decreases, player_kill and player_died are suppressed for that update. There are no per-round assists or exact MVP-award timestamps. The last-authoritative/final match totals also live in the recorder's local_summary. Do not substitute spectator totals.

events.description: CS2 reported an increase in your player's kill total for the current match.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold, known kills for this match increase, and no comparable match-stat counter decreases in the same update.

fields.name: count
fields.description: How many kills were added between the two compared GSI updates. Always positive; can exceed one. If the match kill counter moves from 5 to 7, count is 2.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Your player's CS2-reported kill total for the current match, across all rounds so far. Not kills in this round, since necko7 connected, during this stream or over your lifetime. In the 5 -> 7 example, total is 7.

events.notes: There is no victim, attacker object, weapon-at-kill or headshot flag. Use trustworthy round_stats_changed/current_match round data for headshot and multi-kill conditions. Do not assume one callback per victim, infer an ace from total, or add round_stats_changed to player_kill as if they were independent kills. Identity restoration or a new baseline does not infer missed kills.

events.description: Your player's death is corroborated by health and the death counter for the current match.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold, known health moves from a positive value to zero, deaths for this match increase by exactly one, and no comparable match-stat counter decreases.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Your player's CS2-reported death total for the current match, across all rounds so far. Not deaths this round, since necko7 connected or over your lifetime.

events.notes: Health zero alone, a death counter jump larger than one, or a switch to spectating does not generate this event. No killer, cause, weapon or death location is provided. Absence of an event does not prove survival when the relevant identity/boundary evidence is missing.

events.description: One or both authoritative local round kill counters changed.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold and known round kills/headshot kills differ. Every comparable changed counter is included.

fields.name: changes
fields.description: Non-empty changes for round_kills and/or round_headshot_kills. Each entry contains stat, previous, current and signed delta.

events.notes: Names in this event are round_kills and round_headshot_kills; corresponding state fields are round_stats.kills and round_stats.headshot_kills. Negative observed corrections can appear. A next-round reset is not treated as combat. The recorder retains authoritative values seen before a spectator switch, so completed-round data can be known even when no local player is visible at the end. There are no per-round assists or damage fields.

events.description: The unambiguously selected local weapon changed name or category.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold. Both inventories have exactly one non-holstered weapon (active or reloading), and the selected weapon name or category differs.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current selected identities, each containing name, category and nullable finish.

events.notes: Inventory slot keys are not entity IDs. No weapon event is derived if selection is ambiguous or an inventory is unavailable. A finish-only change does not emit weapon_changed; ammo/status comparison is also suppressed when finishes differ. This is selection, not a pickup/drop/shot event.

events.description: The selected local weapon's observed status changed without changing its identity.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold. Both snapshots have one unambiguous selected weapon; its name, category and finish match, but its status differs.

fields.name: weapon
fields.description: Current selected identity: name, category and nullable finish.

fields.name: change
fields.description: Previous/current normalized status. Vocabulary is active, holstered and reloading; see the selection limitation below.

events.notes: The selected-weapon comparison excludes holstered weapons. Although holstered is a valid normalized inventory status, this event currently derives active <-> reloading transitions; it is not a general event for every inventory status change. Reload status is observed, not a promise that a reload will complete.

events.description: At least one ammo value changed for the same selected local weapon.
events.when: The [local-player comparison rules](#comparison-rules) hold, both snapshots have one unambiguous selected weapon with matching name/category/finish, and at least one ammo value is known in both snapshots and different.

fields.name: weapon
fields.description: Current selected identity: name, category and nullable finish.

fields.name: clip
fields.description: Clip change, or null if unchanged/not comparable.

fields.name: capacity
fields.description: Clip-capacity change, or null if unchanged/not comparable.

fields.name: reserve
fields.description: Reported reserve change, or null if unchanged/not comparable.

events.notes: Ammo deltas are not shot events. Reloads and other changes affect ammo, and reserve units are whatever CS2 reports; do not assume bullets (some captures use magazine-like units). A weapon/finish switch or ambiguous selection suppresses the comparison. Check each nullable change before reading its members.
